The world’s greatest problems propel everything we do. Seraphim is the global leader in SpaceTech investment. We endlessly explore the ecosystem to discover and invest in the brightest minds and smartest ideas which will provide trailblazing, high-value solutions that disrupt, transform and improve life as we know it.

Accelerating humanity’s next giant leap by transforming science fiction into science fact.

we are your mission control

For visionary space entrepreneurs providing them the backing to achieve escape velocity

Across the Seraphim Space investment funds, Seraphim Academy and Seraphim Space Investment Trust, we are the first organisation to support space entrepreneurship from inception to exit. seraphim portfolio launch on spacex bandwagon-5
WRITTEN BY: LEAH MARTIN | OCTOBER 21, 2026
tl;dr / executive summary

SpaceX’s fifth Bandwagon mission deployed new satellites for Xona, ICEYE, Tomorrow.io and HawkEye 360, four Seraphim portfolio companies.
Xona launched six Pulsar satellites, ICEYE added four radar imaging satellites, Tomorrow.io launched two weather satellites, and HawkEye 360 deployed its three-satellite Cluster 15.
The deployments expand capabilities across positioning and navigation, Earth observation, weather forecasting and radio-frequency intelligence.

[Credit: SpaceX]

Tuesday’s fifth SpaceX Bandwagon mission was a particularly busy one for the Seraphim portfolio. Launching from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, the mission saw Xona, ICEYE, Tomorrow.io and HawkEye 360 all successfully deploy new spacecraft.

It’s a great snapshot of where SpaceTech is heading: increasingly capable commercial constellations providing data and infrastructure for mission-critical applications spanning navigation, Earth observation, weather and RF intelligence.

xona deploys first pulsar service cluster

Xona deployed six Pulsar satellites and has made contact with all six. Four form the company’s first service cluster, a major milestone as Xona moves towards demonstrating a new space-based positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) service.

iceye expands sar constellation with four new satellites

ICEYE launched four new synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites, including two for Portugal’s Atlantic Constellation in collaboration with CTI Aeroespacial and the Portuguese Air Force. All four have already begun operations.

SAR’s ability to image through cloud and darkness makes it an increasingly important capability for persistent monitoring, from natural disasters and maritime activity to security and defence.

tomorrow.io accelerates weather constellation build-out

Tomorrow.io, meanwhile, launched its S14 and S15 microwave sounders, its third and fourth launches in just 19 days. The additional capability is helping drive revisit rates below one hour as the company builds out its proprietary weather satellite constellation.


hawkeye 360’s cluster 15 enters operation

Finally, HawkEye 360’s three-satellite Cluster 15 successfully reached orbit and became operational. The latest spacecraft bring advanced antenna capabilities that enable the simultaneous collection of multiple RF signal types, further strengthening HawkEye 360’s space-based RF intelligence capabilities.

There’s more to come, too: HawkEye 360 is eyeing another launch this week, this time with Rocket Lab from New Zealand.

[Credit: SpaceX]

Four companies tackling four very different problems, but with a common theme: increasingly capable infrastructure in orbit delivering increasingly useful intelligence on Earth.

Congratulations to Xona, ICEYE, Tomorrow.io and HawkEye 360.

new investment: mp space raises $16m in seed funding
WRITTEN BY: LEAH MARTIN | OCTOBER 27, 2026
tl;dr / executive summary

MP Space, an Australian spacecraft power technology company founded by ex-Tesla engineers, has raised (US) $16 million in Seed funding.
The raise, one of the largest seed rounds for an Australian deep technology company, marks Seraphim’s first investment in an Australian company.
The round was led by Blackbird, with participation from ourselves, Systemiq Capital, Speedinvest and MFV Partners.
MP Space develops hardware and software that generates, stores and manages power for satellites and other spacecraft.
The funding will enable MP Space to scale local manufacturing, expand its range of power-system platforms, and grow its Australian engineering team.

The MP Space Team

Sydney-based space power technology company MP Space has closed a $23 million (US$16 million) Seed round led by Blackbird, with Seraphim Space, the world’s most prolific investor in space, making its first-ever investment in an Australian company. 

The raise, one of the largest seed rounds for an Australian deep technology company, will enable MP Space to scale local manufacturing, expand its range of power-system platforms, and grow its Australian engineering team. 

The investment highlights the strategic importance of the Federal Government’s Statement on Space, which sets out the national focus areas: Trusted Space Services, Spaceflight  Ecosystem, Space Platforms, Microgravity Ecosystem and Exploration Technologies. MP Space’s power infrastructure underpins each of the five areas, supplying the reliable, fit-for-purpose power every satellite, launch vehicle and lunar mission depends on to operate. The scale of the seed round reinforces the increased confidence investors have in Australia in the wake of the Federal Government releasing the strategic agenda for the space industry.  

The round was led by Blackbird, with participation from Systemiq Capital, Seraphim Space, Speedinvest and MFV Partners, bringing together Australian and international investors to support MP Space’s next phase of growth.

Founded in January 2024 by former Tesla engineers Jay Manley (CEO) and Sam Paterson  (CCO), MP Space has already been designed into several space services and missions,  totalling more than 500 spacecraft, with its hardware in orbit in October 2026 on multiple spacecraft.

MP Space has been a resident of the NSW Government-backed National Defence and  Aerospace Hub (formerly National Space Industry Hub) at Cicada Innovations for over two  years, presenting at Cicada x Tech23 in Sydney on 9 September 2026 alongside this year’s  cohort of Australian deep-tech ventures.

Jay Manley, CEO and Co-Founder, MP Space said: 

“Our thesis is simple: the next generation of spacecraft will need a lot more power, and the  space industry needs better ways to generate, store and manage it. 

“We’ve seen enormous advances in power electronics, software and energy storage through  electric vehicles, grid-scale energy and home batteries. MP Space is bringing that same  advanced technology to spacecraft power systems, designed from the outset to be  manufactured reliably and at scale. 

This raise reflects the customer demand we’re already seeing and gives us the capital to  accelerate. Over the next 12 months, our focus is expanding manufacturing capacity, scaling  the team and delivering power systems for the next generation of spacecraft and constellations.” 

Samantha Wong, Partner at Blackbird said: 

“At Blackbird, our investment conviction starts with the founding team. Jay and Sam have gone  from solar racecar clubs at uni to industry-leading capability in scalable battery system design,  having built Tesla’s Powerwall from electrons to a $10 billion businessline. The same energy  management evolution will happen in space and we believe MP Space has a shot at  revolutionising this fast-growing industry. 

“In less than two years, MP Space has already delivered a software-defined battery, with one of the highest gravimetric energy densities of any space battery, and will gain flight heritage this month. They are moving with speed and precision in a market that has explosive potential.  

“As space unlocks more use cases, MP Space is well-placed to seize the opportunity with an indisputable hardware advantage and deep software capabilities. It’s an Aussie business redefining the global standard. These are the types of businesses we are proud to back.” 

Lucas Bishop, Vice President at Seraphim Space said: 

“We’re excited to back Jay Manley, Sam Paterson and the broader MP Space team as they build the next generation of spacecraft power systems. Drawing on their experience scaling some of the world’s most demanding energy and power hardware programmes at Tesla, the team is exceptionally well placed to address two fundamental challenges facing the space industry. 

“Power is a fundamental constraint on spacecraft capability, and we are seeing power requirements scale rapidly across almost every mission type. More available power directly enables more capable payloads, greater onboard processing and, ultimately, more  ambitious missions. 

“Separately, the industry lacks proven, independent suppliers capable of delivering critical hardware reliably and at scale. This has made vertical integration a necessity rather than a choice for spacecraft manufacturers. By replacing bespoke, high-cost and low-volume systems with reliable, cost-effective and off-the-shelf power hardware, MP Space can help reverse this historical over-reliance on vertical integration. 

“We believe this positions MP Space to become a foundational supplier to the next generation of spacecraft, and we’re delighted to support the team on that journey.” 

Dan Lloyd, CEO, Space Industry Association of Australia said: 

“The Space Industry Association of Australia (SIAA) is delighted to see one of our members, MP  Space, moving forward so quickly to commercialise such a strategic niche which underpins the success of the entire industry. We can get fixated on the many visually impressive technologies in the space industry, especially rockets and satellites, but we cannot forget that in the end our economic resilience and Future Made in Australia will depend upon our ability to build, maintain  and replenish the critical inputs, such as reliable, fit-for-purpose and efficient power systems. 

“The momentum that Australia is building across the sector right now is demonstrating that government, industry and the international markets all recognise the unique potential for  Australia in space. We have unparalleled clear skies, massive open test facilities, and top global engineering talent. With the Ministerial Statement on Space and the raft of activity across  National Security and Defence, Australia is rapidly developing the policy vision which will drive  there.” 

Liza Noonan, CEO, Cicada Innovations said: 

“Cicada Innovations is delighted to see MP Space – a NSW Defence and Aerospace Hub resident and Cicada x Tech23 venture – reach such a significant milestone that demonstrates the capability Australia’s space industry possesses. 

“The company’s evolution underscores the Hub’s value in advancing Australia’s space industry,  providing the specialist support and facilities required to build successful ventures.”
